title: 2002 HMMT February Team Problem 10
statement: Exhibit a configuration of the board and a choice of \(s_{1}\) and \(s_{2}\) so that \(s_{1}>s_{2}\), yet the second player wins with probability strictly greater than \(\frac{1}{2}\).

solutions.text: Let \(s_{1}=3\) and \(s_{2}=2\) and place an arrow on all the even-numbered squares. In this configuration, player 1 can move at most six squares in a turn: up to three from his roll and an additional three if his roll landed him on an arrow. Hence player 1 cannot win on his first or second turn. Player 2, however, wins immediately if she ever lands on an arrow. Thus player 2 has probability \(1 / 2\) of winning on her first turn, and failing that, she has probability \(1 / 2\) of winning on her second turn. Hence player 2 wins with probability at least \(1 / 2+(1 / 2)(1 / 2)=3 / 4\).
